fatal_errors: It attributes disappearance of the smallest particles primarily to Ostwald ripening and redeposition, whereas the target mechanism emphasizes Au/Cu surface segregation followed by shell melting and evaporation.
It predicts evolution from spherical to faceted or irregular particles, opposite to the observed elliptical-to-spherical reshaping.
The asserted greater-than-50-nm boundary for sluggish diffusion is unsupported and misses the experimentally relevant onset of active segregation near 673 K.
explanation: The hypothesis captures the central finding that diffusion is not sluggish in sub-10 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles and that surface-energy differences drive Au/Cu enrichment under vacuum heating. It also provides a broadly suitable in situ TEM-compositional test. However, it omits the initial multi-twinned/icosahedral state, PLD preparation at 873 K, the 1 K/s heating protocol and stepped temperatures. More importantly, it substitutes Ostwald ripening for the target melting/evaporation pathway and predicts the wrong direction of shape evolution. Its boundary is speculative rather than tied to the approximately 673 K onset and shape/size dependence. The cited evidence concerns unrelated bulk HEA systems and does not validate diffusion, segregation, or evaporation in these nanoparticles.
